articles.text: LIÚ YUÈWÉN: Jīntian cānguānle Gùgōng hái bú gòu lèi ma? Hái zài zhèr kàn dìtú ne!
LIÚ YUÈWÉN: Aren't you tired enough after visiting the Palace Museum today? Still here reading maps!
BÓNÀJĪ: Ā! Shi nǐ ya? Lái lái lái, zài zhèr zuò yìhuǐr. Nǐ hē shénme? Kāfēi?
BERNACKI: Ah, it's you? Come on and sit down here for a while. What are you drinking? Coffee?
LIÚ YUÈWÉN: Ǹg, shi kāfēi. Wǒ zài Déguóde shíhou hēchéng xíguàn le.
LIÚ YUÈWÉN: Yes, coffee. I got in the habit of drinking it when I was in Germany.
BÓNÀJĪ: Duì le. Wǒ zěnme huì wàngle nǐ shi zài Déguó xuéde jiànzhù. Huí guó zhème duō nián, méiyou zài qùguo Ōuzhōu?
BERNACKI: Oh yes; how could I forget that you studied architecture in Germany. After so many years back in China, haven't you gone back to Europe at all?
LIÚ YUÈWÉN: Yòu qùguo yícì, nèi shi qīJiǔnián, zhèicì bǐ shàngcì duō zǒule jǐge dìfang.
LIÚ YUÈWÉN: I've been back once. That was in '79. That time I went to a few more places than the previous time.
BÓNÀJĪ: Shéi qùguo Ōuzhōu, shéi jiù huì xiǎngzhe ta. Jiù xiàng Zhōngguó yíyàng, láiguo Zhōngguóde rén, bù guǎn shénme shíhou, zǒng hái huì xiǎngzhe ta.
BERNACKI: Whoever goes to Europe will always think of it. It's just like China, no matter when it is that a person comes here, they'll always think of it.
LIÚ YUÈWÉN: Shì!... Gāngcái wǒ láide shíhour, nǐ hǎoxiàng zài yánjiū shénme?
LIÚ YUÈWÉN: Yes, indeed!... Just now when I came, you seemed to be studying something, is that so?
BÓNÀJĪ: Méi shénme, wǒ zài xiǎng, Běijīngde dìxíng hé ná Běijīng zuò shǒudū yǒu diǎnr guānxi.
BERNACKI: Nothing much. I was thinking that the topography of Běijīng has something to do with using it as the capital.
LIÚ YUÈWÉN: Nǐ shuōde duì, Běijīng zài Huáběi Píngyuánde zuì běibiān, xīběi kào shān, dōng, nán shi píngyuán.
LIÚ YUÈWÉN: That's right. Běijīng is in the northernmost part of the North China Plain. On the northwest it is bordered by mountains; to the east and south there are flatlands.
BÓNÀJĪ: Zhèizhǒng dìxíng ràng rén gǎnjué bǐjiào róngyi fángbèi běifāng láide qīnlüè.
BERNACKI: This kind of topography made people feel as if it were easier to guard against invasions from the north.
LIÚ YUÈWÉN: Tèbié shi yǒule Chángchéng yǐhòu, gèng róngyi fángbèi.
LIÚ YUÈWÉN: Especially after the Great Wall was built, it was even easier to guard against invasions.
BÓNÀJĪ: Tīngshuō Chángchéng xiūguo bù zhīdào duōshǎo cì le.
BERNACKI: I understand the Great Wall has been repaired I-don't-know how many times.
LIÚ YUÈWÉN: Cóng Qíncháo dào xiànzài, Chángchéng yìzhí zài xiū, wǒmen děi jìde bù guǎn shénme shíhour wǒmen dōu děi xiǎoxīn běifāng láide qīnlüè!
LIÚ YUÈWÉN: From the Qín dynasty down to the present the Great Wall has been under repair all along. We must remember that no matter when, we must always beware of invasion from the north!
BÓNÀJĪ: Nǐ zhēn yǒu yìsi. Duì le, wǒ xiǎng wǒmen qiántian qù kànguode nèiduàn Chángchéng hǎoxiàng bú shi Qíncháo jiànzhùde?
BERNACKI: You're such a card. Oh yes--it seems to me that the section of the Great Wall we went to see the day before yesterday wasn't built during the Qín dynasty, was it?

LIÚ YUÈWÉN: Ǹg, shi Míngcháo chóngxīn jiànzhùde. Qíncháode Chángchéng zài Bādálǐng běibian liǎngbǎiduō lǐde dìfang. Suǒyǐ lái Zhōngguó cānguānde wàiguó péngyou píngcháng kàndàode Chángchéng bú shi zuì lǎode yíduàn.

LIÚ YUÈWÉN: Mm, it was rebuilt in the Míng Dynasty. The Qín Dynasty Great Wall is over two hundred li north of Bādálǐng. So the Great Wall that foreign friends who come to sightsee in China usually see isn't the oldest section.
BÓNÀJĪ: "Wànlǐ Chángchéng" zhēn yǒu yíwàn lǐ cháng ma?
BERNACKI: Is the "Great Wall of Ten Thousand Li" really ten thousand li long?
LIÚ YUÈWÉN: Yǒu, Chángchéng jīngguòle qīge shěng, yígòng yǒu yíwàn èrqiān lǐ cháng.
LIÚ YUÈWÉN: Yes. The Great Wall passes through seven provinces and altogether is 12,000 li long.
BÓNÀJĪ: Chúle Chángchéng yǐwài, wǒmen jǐge jiànzhù gōngzuòzhě duì Shísānlíngde dìxià gōngdiàn yě hěn yǒu xìngqu.
BERNACKI: Besides the Great Wall, we building workers are also very interested in the underground palaces of the Thirteen Tombs.
LIÚ YUÈWÉN: Tándào Zhōngguó gǔdài jiànzhù yìshu, nǐ qùguo Tiāntán ma? Nǐmende yóulǎn jìhuali yǒu méiyou Tiāntán?
LIÚ YUÈWÉN: Speaking of ancient Chinese architectural art, have you been to the Temple of Heaven? Is that on your touring schedule?
BÓNÀJĪ: Ō, duì le, Tiāntán! Wǒ xiǎngqilai le, tīngshuō Tiāntán gàide hěn tèbié. Kěshi, bù zhīdào wèishénme, wǒmende yóulǎn jìhuali hǎoxiàng méiyǒu.
BERNACKI: Oh, yes--the Temple of Heaven. That reminds me. I've heard that the Temple of Heaven is very special. But for some reason I don't know, it doesn't seem to be on our tour schedule.
LIÚ YUÈWÉN: Bú yàojǐnde. Wǒmen hé Zhōngguó Lǚxíngshè tányitán, rúguǒ tāmen méiyou shíjiān ānpáide huà, wǒmen kěyi zài Xīngqītiān zìjǐ qù.
LIÚ YUÈWÉN: That doesn't matter. We'll talk about it with the China Travel Service, and if they don't have time to set it up, we can go by ourselves on Sunday.
BÓNÀJĪ: Xīngqītiān zìjǐ qù! Hǎo jìhua! Nǐde xiānsheng, háizi, dōu kěyi lái ma?
BERNACKI: Go ourselves on Sunday! That's a great plan! Can your husband and children all come too?
LIÚ YUÈWÉN: Dàgài kěyi. Wǒ àiren hé wǒde dà érzi dōu shi gǎo jiànzhùde, tāmen kěyi gěi ni hǎohāor jièshao yìxiē Tiāntánde jiànzhù tèdiǎn.
LIÚ YUÈWÉN: Probably. My spouse and my oldest son are both in building. They can do a proper job of showing you the special architectural characteristics of the Temple of Heaven.
BÓNÀJĪ: Wǒmen zěnme qù ne?
BERNACKI: How shall we go there?
LIÚ YUÈWÉN: Nǐ xiǎng bu xiǎng zǒuyizǒu a?
LIÚ YUÈWÉN: Do you want to walk a little?
BÓNÀJĪ: Kěyi a! Zài shuō, wǒ xiǎng Xīngqītiānde gōnggòng qìchē dàgài xiāngdāng jǐ.
BERNACKI: That would be okay. Besides, I suppose the buses are pretty crowded on Sundays.
LIÚ YUÈWÉN: Ǹg. Wǒmen cóng Běijīng Fàndiàn zǒu dào Tiān'ānmén, ránhòu chuānguò guǎngchǎng, bù yuǎn jiù shi Tiāntán le.
LIÚ YUÈWÉN: Mm. From the Běijīng Hotel we walk to the Gate of Heavenly Peace, then we cross the square, and not far from there is the Temple of Heaven.
BÓNÀJĪ: Hǎo, jiù zhème juédìng le. Búguò, bù zhīdào Tiāntán yǒu duō dà? Bàntiān kàndewán ma?
BERNACKI: Okay. Then that's the decision. Only, I wonder how large the Temple of Heaven is? Could we see it in half a day?
LIÚ YUÈWÉN: Tiāntán bǐ Yíhéyuán xiǎode duō, zhǔyàode jiànzhù jiù yǒu liǎngbùfen. Bàntiān dàgài kěyi kànwán. Zěnme, Xīngqītiān nǐ hái yǒu biéde shì ma?

LIÚ YUÈWÉN: The Temple of Heaven is much smaller than the Summer Palace. The main structures include only two parts. You can probably finish seeing it in half a day. Why? Do you have other things to do on Sunday?
BÓNÀJĪ: Xīngqītiān xiàwǔ yǒu rén qǐng wǒmen chī fàn. Bù hǎo yìsi bú qù, kěshi xīnshǎng jiànzhù yìshu, nà kě shi yàojǐnde shìr, bàntiān dàgài bú gòu!

BERNACKI: Sunday afternoon we've been invited to dinner. It would be embarrassing if we didn't go, but admiring architectural art is certainly an important thing, and half a day probably won't be enough!
LIÚ YUÈWÉN: Bú yàojǐnde, zhèige Xīngqītiān wǒmen zǎo diǎnr qù. Zǎo qù zǎo huí, jiù kàn bàntiān. Rúguǒ nǐ hái xiǎng qù, wǒmen zài xiǎng bànfǎ yuē shíjiān.
LIÚ YUÈWÉN: That's okay, this Sunday we'll go a little earlier. We'll leave early and come back early, and just spend half a day there. If you still want to go we'll try to arrange a time.
BÓNÀJĪ: Hǎo, jiù zhèiyang le. Wǒ jìde zài Ōuzhōu cānguān yíge jiàotáng nà děi yòng duō shǎo shíjiān ne!
BERNACKI: Okay, that sounds good. I remember it takes quite a long time to tour a cathedral in Europe!
LIÚ YUÈWÉN: Hǎo le, jiù zhèiyangr. Xīngqītiān zǎoshang bādiǎn, zài lóuxia dà ménkǒur jiàn, rúguǒ yǒu shénme gǎibiàn, wǒ zài dǎ diànhuà gěi nǐ.
LIÚ YUÈWÉN: All right, that's our plan. We'll meet at the entrance downstairs, Sunday morning at eight. If there's any change I'll give you a call.
BÓNÀJĪ: Hǎode, jiù zhèiyang!
BERNACKI: Okay, that's fine!
